parsed.doc_summary: Law-firm alert on California AB 325 / SB 763 amending the Cartwright Act (effective 2026-01-01), banning use/distribution of common pricing algorithms in restraint of trade and coercing adoption of recommendations. Applies statewide to all businesses incl. rental housing; no local-city laws described.

rules.title: Cartwright Act amendments on common pricing algorithms (AB 325 / SB 763)
rules.requirement: Businesses may not use or distribute a common pricing algorithm (two or more users, uses competitor data) as part of an agreement to restrain trade, or use/offer one while coercing users to adopt its price recommendations. Single-firm algorithms using only the business's own data are not covered.
rules.key_value: ban on common pricing algorithms using competitor data to collude or coerce
rules.quoted_span: Businesses are expressly prohibited from using or distributing common pricing algorithms as part of an agreement to restrain trade.
rules.effective_date_note: Alert states the laws took effect January 1, 2026; signed October 2025.
rules.penalty: Criminal fines up to $6 million (corporations) or $1 million (individuals), or twice gain/loss if greater; civil fines up to $1 million in AG/DA actions; treble damages and attorneys' fees in private suits.
rules.exemptions: Algorithms using only a business's own data.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all businesses, including apartment rental companies using common pricing software.
